provenance.built_from: the fixture's required_beats, read against the source text (Lang, The Blue Fairy Book (PG #503)) and the event definition in src/extraction/pass-events.ts
provenance.blind_to: whether a candidate matched the beat. The classification was made from the beat and the definition; the recorded runs were consulted only afterwards, to compute the numbers.
provenance.author: hand-annotated (a manual read, not a judge pass — a judge pass can replace it and be compared against it)

inclusion_rule.definition: pass-events.ts: "An event is one thing that HAPPENS or CHANGES: an action, an arrival, a decision made aloud, a death, a transformation, a promise. Not a description, not a mood, not a standing fact."
inclusion_rule.non_eventful_when: the beat, as the fixture words it, contains no action, speech act, arrival or change of state or knowledge at all
eventful_when: the beat contains any happening, even alongside a mood or a description
in doubt — a beat is excluded only when it is clearly not an event, so the list errs toward a larger denominator and a lower recall_eventful
inclusion_rule.note: Classified by the beat as written, not by what the source narrates nearby. This says nothing about whether the beat matters to the story — "Cinderella does not ask to go" matters a great deal — only about whether an extractor obeying its own prompt can emit it.

non_eventful.text: the father has remarried a proud and haughty woman
non_eventful.why: The situation the story opens on, given in the pluperfect. The source does narrate the marriage in its first sentence, which is why this one is marked low: an extractor reading it as a "past" event would not be wrong.

non_eventful.text: her two daughters prove as haughty as their mother
non_eventful.why: What the daughters are like. Nothing happens.

non_eventful.text: the two sisters are overjoyed and think of nothing but what to wear
non_eventful.why: How the sisters feel and what occupies them.

non_eventful.text: Cinderella is expected to help them dress but is not imagined as a guest herself
non_eventful.why: What the household assumes, and what it fails to imagine. Not a happening.

non_eventful.text: Cinderella does not ask to go
no one — including her own stepmother and sisters — recognizes her
non_eventful.why: A recognition that does not occur.

non_eventful.text: the sisters do not know her
non_eventful.why: The same absence of recognition as scene_06#3, restated for the sisters.

non_eventful.text: she says nothing of the ball to anyone in the household

borderline_kept_eventful.text: she is so happy she loses all track of time
borderline_kept_eventful.why: A feeling, but its content is a change with consequences: she stops tracking the hour. Kept.

borderline_kept_eventful.text: of all her finery, only the fellow glass slipper remains, kept in her pocket
borderline_kept_eventful.why: Reads as a state ("remains"), but it is the outcome of the reversion one beat earlier and of her keeping the slipper. Kept, since excluding it is the generous reading.
